name: M10 an old version of a document is not replaced (two entries for one document)

why: argued equivalent: the read of the text does not touch the memo (the thunk is `getText()` of a document), so the index cannot move; the same answer in every row

name: M12 the dead entries are not pruned

name: M13 the prune drops the LIVE entries
why: nothing is ever kept; killed by document-text-memo.test.ts

name: M14 the entry is matched by the WeakRef, not its target

from: entries.push({ document: new WeakRef(document), version, text });
to: entries.push({ document: new WeakRef(document), version: version + 1, text });

name: M16 the text stored is trimmed
from: entries.push({ document: new WeakRef(document), version, text });
to: entries.push({ document: new WeakRef(document), version, text: text.trim() });

name: M17 the text is read twice
why: the count rows; killed by document-text-memo.test.ts

name: M18 a throwing read is swallowed
why: the error does not propagate, and an empty text is stored; killed by document-text-memo.test.ts

name: M19 a hit answers the first entry, not the document's
why: two documents are answered the same text; killed by document-text-memo.test.ts

name: M20 an eviction test with `if` for the `while` (one push per call, so the same)
why: argued equivalent: one entry is pushed per call, so the loop runs at most once and `if` keeps the same entries

name: M22 the version is truncated to a whole number
why: 1.5 and 1 share an entry: a fraction version is served another version's text (the oracle draws fractions); killed by document-text-memo.test.ts

name: M23 a collected-entry test reads a document that is not there
why: the WeakRef object itself is never undefined, so nothing is pruned: the same as M12; killed by document-text-memo.test.ts
